title: MZ Tales of Frah'Akin RPG [UPDATED DEMO 2.0]

posts.author: Aeghite
posts.body:
Tales of Frah’Akin is an upcoming story-based fantasy RPG, in the style of the old classics but with a modern touch, rich with cinematic cutscenes.
Steam:
https://bit.ly/46S7fBg
Itch:
https://bit.ly/3YQe7wQ
Tales of Frah’Akin will be available on Steam and Itch. There's also a Kickstarter campaign in the making.​
​
Step into the role of Ennea, princess of the Forest Elves, and embark on a journey across the magical land of Frah’Akin. Uncover the secrets of a looming threat that endangers the elven realm, forge bonds with unique companions, and reveal hidden truths about the past, present, and future. Your choices will shape the world around you — and the people in it!
In special scenes, you’ll even get to play as other main characters, diving into their personal memories and perspectives. Romance, friendship, conflict — every relationship holds the power to change the course of your story.
NO random encounters! See your opponents ahead of time, then choose who to fight.
Use combo skills to take down enemies fast.
Auto battle for farming and fast leveling up.
Discover more about the world and people around you through interactions and side quests. Learn backstories and secrets of the past.
Exploration & rewards
– Find hidden treasures, uncover secrets, and enjoy various
mini-games
including:
Fishing
Playing instruments
Dancing
Training animals
Matching card games
Chess
Mining
Gather ingredients, learn how to craft items, and even make your own equipment.
​
13 playable characters, each with a unique skill set, personal questline, and backstory.
Two outfit sets per character.
A variety of interactive mini-games.
No random encounters! Choose your battles strategically.
Custom hand-drawn art, including scene-based CGs and expressive character busts.
Original soundtrack with a captivating, fairy-tale-like main theme.
Character interactions & potential romances.
English & Polish language support.
Fully voice-acted demo.
35-40h of content.
DEMO is live!
​

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I gave your demo a few tries and managed to make it to the end of the v1.2 demo. I enjoyed playing and am looking forward to seeing where this goes next, so great job! That said, the polish that's in a lot of the game does make some of the rougher things stand out. From what I've seen in this demo, I think you can do even better so if it sounds like I'm being nitpicky about certain things, it's because I am.
Spoiler:
Feedback
I'll start with some of the stuff I really liked. The art is lovely, the voice acting was a nice touch (though I do have thoughts), and the maps clearly have lots of time and love put into them. There are a lot of hints at mysteries in the story, and while the demo doesn't go too in-depth it does have some good hooks. I also liked that you had quite a few little details and minigame hidden around the starting village to teach players to explore without coming out and going "look around you fools!" in a message box. And I was honestly disappointed when the demo ended because I wanted to keep playing and see how Thomas would fit into my battle style.
That said, there were things that I think need more work. I found the game stuttering and dropping below 20FPS on certain outside maps (though it usually ran fine indoors and on other outdoor maps), so I don't know what is going on but it was a rough introduction to the game when I was slowly walking around the first map. I tried turning off the screen effects in the Options menu, but that didn't seem to really affect the FPS unfortunately. I'm guessing it's related to either parallel processes or a plugin, so you may want to double-check the starting map to see if there's something odd there that is used on other maps too.
I do like that you have an icon when you approach an item that can be interacted with, but since you have to be right next to the event and facing it it's easy to miss something unless you're rubbing your face against everything. I think there's a balance you could find between the current method and having an icon fully visible at all times. Maybe the icon appears when you're within 3 tiles of the event, or opening the map will also mark interactable spots. Two spots where I really think this issue is a big problem is in item shops and when finding plants in the wild. The first time I played I didn't even realize that the item shop had Potions and Magic Water for sale! The shopkeeper didn't have them as an option in his menu, so you could only buy those if you went to the back of the shop and interacted with the bottles on the table, which I thought were just decorations since the table right in front of the door didn't have anything you could click on. In a situation like that, I think it would be best if the shop's for-sale items were clearly laid out or always marked with an icon so that players can easily tell what they could buy. And when it come to finding plants in the wild, I found that some of the grasses were used as normal decorations under trees so I would think there was another I could collect but it turned out I couldn't reach it. Collectable plants could really use icons that appear when the player is a few tiles away, or some subtle sparkles to draw the player's eye.
I love minigames and crafting systems, so imagine my delight when I realized this game has quite a few! Unfortunately it felt like some of them were more of an afterthought in this demo, and it may have been better to leave them out until a later demo or the full release. I only found the Fishing Rod during my 3rd playthrough (didn't realize Senersis' house was down the previously closed road), and while I liked it I didn't really need to eat any fish while playing. The card matching minigame I did enjoy, but I didn't realize that I needed to use my mouse for it at first so I was just clicking on my keys and wondering why nothing was happening. I think the music minigame was the weakest one I played, for two reasons: first, I play with the sound off because I get headaches from game sounds easily, and second, it was a very long introduction to the minigame. The first point isn't something you can really fix, just have to keep in mind that not everyone can or will hear musical cues, but I think the second one could be easily fixed. Shorten that first music minigame by half, and that should help players learn how the minigame works without it feeling overwhelming.
The crafting system really disappointed me. I was excited when I first got a recipe thanks to a side quest, but that was the only one I found. Considering the number of plants I found, I know there are more recipes in the game but I was never poisoned in battle so being able to make a few Antidotes didn't really help. Perhaps later in the game it will be useful, but for an introduction to the crafting system it felt like the game was telling me "here is a system that you won't be using"... I think if you're going to have crafting, then giving a Potion recipe early may be better. I didn't really use items in battle at all since HP and MP seemed to be healed after most fights, but a Potion would be a lot more helpful early in the game than an Antidote.
Speaking of using items in battles, I think battles were the weakest point in this entire demo. They were
fine
, but compared to the rest of the demo they didn't feel as polished. The normal enemies were easy enough to defeat just with Ennea using magic and Aehlevander using his normal attack, so I rarely used Aehlevander's support spells. The fact that they could only target one party member at a time was definitely another reason I didn't use them often, since by the time I had buffed both of them the battle was usually over. So imagine my surprise when I went through every fight before the wolf boss battle, and the boss fight kicked my butt almost instantly! I understand boss fights should be challenging, but its Multiscratch attack could do more damage than Ennea could stand, so early in the battle she would be dead and I'd need to revive her. I did all I could, buffing their defense and attacks, using the strongest spells I had access to, using their combo skills, and I still got a game over. It ended up that I needed to leave the map so all the enemies respawned so I could fight them all again and level up more before I stood a chance, and even then Ennea died a few times. I honestly thought I wasn't supposed to win that fight the first time, just because of how much HP the boss had and how deadly its attacks were. A challenging boss battle is fine, but I think the Multscratch attack needs tweaked so that it's not a one-hit KO for Ennea, since she is the main damage dealer.
The skills all worked, but I feel like I must've been missing something when using them. The Fire spell was strong so I used it often, but for some reason the state that is applied made the enemy resistant to fire attacks? For normal enemies it didn't really matter since I could still kill them with normal attacks after that first spell, but I expected enemies to be weaker to flames when on fire or maybe take more damage from the nature spells. It would have been cool if the different types of magic had an effect that could boost or weaken other types of magic, so players would need to think before casting spells willy-nilly. Aehlevander only gained one debuffing skill while I played, Slow, so I didn't see how debuffs could help in battles much but I do think him buffing the party one turn and then debuffing the enemies the next turn could really turn the tides in harder battles. Most of the normal enemies seemed to lack weaknesses to any elements (besides the foxes, who seemed resistant to nature spells), so I didn't really have to plan out my attacks beyond "hit hard and hit fast". If elemental weaknesses will be important later in the game, it would be good to have some enemies that clearly were weak to Ennea's nature spells just so players get it into their head that they should think before clicking a skill.
There were a few other bugs and oddities. Since I did play at least the beginning of v1.0, v1.1, and v1.2, I'll mark the errors with the version I found them in just in case you've already fixed some of them and I missed it:
Why are the blue elves called just the blue elves, compared to luminous or forest elves?
[v1.0] Opening a map with 'tab' is a cool effect, but you may want to turn off mouse-control when it's up since it looks like you're clicking one spot on the map but it's actually just moving you on the map
[v1.0] Can use both Cat and Dog Food from the menu (they're listed as Battle Items), just deleting them from existence
It's cute that feeding cats and dogs gives a boost, but it looks like they can't exist together? May be kinder on players to warn them that feeding one will remove the other regen. And sleeping and walking around wipes it out too, so it doesn't really seem worthwhile
The floor in the castle is incredibly shiny since items on the wall are reflected, which makes it odd that the people don't have reflections
Balloons are very high above the sprites' heads, consider using a plugin to move them closer to the tops of the heads
[v1.0] The music minigame is neat, but you should cover what keys will possibly be included in the game before it starts. The sudden 'W's and 'Q's threw me off. Also it really could do with some visuals as well. Players can hear the good/bad SEs, but a little pop of cheery green would add more visual interest while playing
[v1.1] A minor thing, but changing the unicorn's hitbox to be wider so you can interact with him face-to-face instead of getting right next to his body would look nice
The part of town to the left of the castle (with NPC Martin de Visee) does not have a compass
Door above Martin de Visee is set to 'above character'. Same with the house north of that one. Oh, all the houses on this map suffer from the door problem
[v1.1] The card matching game is a neat idea, but it requires the use of the mouse. Make sure the player knows that when going into the minigame! Would also be good to have a counter so players know how many chances they have left
[v1.1] The statue that gives a boost in the forest to the right of the castle has an 'undefined' message
[v1.1] I turned Battle Voices off in the settings, but they still play if I have Voice Volume on
[v1.1] While I do like knowing the enemy's sight range, the bright red is a bit distracting. Maybe tone it down a bit, or have an option to turn it off?
[v1.2] The fish item descriptions go out of the screen
[v1.2] Senersis is mentioned by the King's assistant, but he isn't mentioned again so it's easy to miss visiting his house. Instead of a message saying not to go that way, have Ennea mention Senersis lives that way, but she needs to visit her father first before saying goodbye
[v1.2] Reading Midgar's letter on his bed ends with Ennea's picture flipping in the middle of the screen randomly
[v1.2] Trying to use the Scroll of Healing on Ennea has an 'undefined' message
Can be selected in battle: Fishing Rod, Midgar's Letter, Pet Foods, Experience Orb, Note III. In fact, a number of non-battle items are marked as usable in battle
While I understand why you set it up this way, Aehlevander congratulates Ennea for using her magic even if she doesn't attack the first turn in the tutorial battle. May want a check in there to make sure Ennea has damaged an enemy first
On the map with the tutorial battle, Ennea can go under the grass and vines on the left side of the river
On that same map, fishing bubbles appear in the upper left corner of the screen, far from the water
Treasure chests stay on the map & compass even after they've been opened, maybe have them change to an open icon instead
The fishing minigames in the forest don't have the "want to fish?" message, it just has the yes/no choice. Could have a Fish/Not now choice instead
Interacting the the dead wolf makes it disappear, but the tile is still blocked by its body
Can walk on the stone statue in Renevia village, near the well
At the farm shop, items with 'undefined' descriptions: Red Pepper, Tomato, Peas, Broccoli, Garlic, Pumpkin
Can't walk through some of the moving yellow flowers near the cemetery
The ground herb plant behind the gravestones gives a Potion, not a plant
Overall, this demo is great! I think there are parts that could used tweaked, especially that first boss fight, but that's more of a case of polishing and balancing instead of needing to fully rework things. I'm looking forward to seeing where this game goes next, so in the future if you need a beta tester to find where something breaks please let me know.
Good luck with your project!

I know this is an early build and stuff so I think you'll be able to get the kinks out and make a really cool and beautiful game.

Here's my review of the demo!
The opening intro was totally unwatchable for me, it lagged/buffered so much. And in the game I too suffered from performance drops (5-year-old laptop, might have helped if I tried changing some graphics card options to use more power). The FPS in the outside areas was around 25-30 and in battles slightly less.
The graphics were cool. Really nice mapping with the varied trees and the buildings blending with the forest. Good character busts. Not the biggest fan of the walking sprites, but they did fit with the game. Good atmosphere with the music and BGS.
Voice acting was ok (except some NPCs sounded a bit weird/monotone). Kind of soft-spoken, but I guess that's a design choice for the elven race. Still I think they could have shown a bit more emotion when saving that girl for example. And is it a design choice or an error that the lips move only at the very start when they speak their lines?
Also, I'd change the menu/cursor/select/cancel rtp(?) sound effects.
Battles were good, basic jrpg battles. Maybe a bit too many enemies resisted/were immune to your forest magic though and the bees had quite a lot of hp and high evasion for early level characters. The wolf boss was quite tough (at least when I hadn't fought many monsters/gained levels before it), I had to use some items, but I thought it was nice to have some challenge in the beginning too. I think that the enemies' hit animation started before their attack motion though and I'm personally not a fan of the longish pre-skill-use light animation. Also, the on map enemies followed you for quite some time, so if you tried to evade them and ran into a "dead end", you might have to fight multiple enemies in a row when getting out.
Lastly some random things:
-after changing your clothes you can run past the unicorn guy to advance the story without talking to him
-Maritee shouted "Wait princess..." when I was walking toward the king and not yet leaving the room
-nice that you had some interactable objects in the houses
-i'd do a quick fade to black when an npc is supposed to leave and do something (like giving the antidote to the girl)
-if I already have a fetch-quest item, I'd make the character comment to the quest giver that they've already got what is needed
-the sprite sometimes flashed when going up the ladders to the treehouses
-the unicorn guy sprite also sometimes flashed/jumped when returning from battles to the map screen
-after killing the wolf boss I ran back to the fountain and then came back, and the boss sprite was kind of sitting on top of the trees (is that on purpose?)
-I wouldn't have the main characters use hp/mp in their speech, but instead just say that the fountain rejuvenates them or something
-at some point the music stopped (didn't loop?) at Master Fenlisher's house (when returning from the basement)
-shouldn't the farmer dudes be more surprised at seeing elves/magical creatures with weird clothing?
Good luck with the project!

@Aeghite
I wanted to cover Tales of Frah'akin because it looked quite promising. The Feedback Festival helped push me to make this review, but trust me when I say I would have picked it out regardless.
--
Spoiler:
Tales of Frah'Akin Review
Spoiler:
Pros
+
Very nice title screen, especially with the fact the characters are slightly animated with the wind blowing and the sky in the back moving.
+
Pretty star animation after selecting new game.
+
Like that you can skip the opening crawl if you don't want to deal with it.
+
As for the opening crawl itself, it's kind of insane to me what you can pull off with RPG Maker. The lore itself is pretty cool and the way it looks is sick.
+
Autosave is always good, even if I feel it's a bit excessive to autosave every time you leave the menu or go to another map.
+
The overworld sprites for the characters are quite adorable, and I like how there's lip motions for the characters when they're talking in cutscenes.
+
I like that there's a quest journal thing that tells you what to do next, as well as a compass. Not my cup of tea, but it could be useful for telling the player where to go next.
+
This mapping is actually quite gorgeous. There's so much detail stacked into every corner.
+
I gave cat food out of the goodness of my heart and got an MP Regen orb. Nice.
+
I'm not sure if this is an MZ thing for Visustella, but starting immediately on the equip slots for items without having to fumble with an obnoxious Equip-Optimize-Clear-Finish menu is very nice.
+
Ooh, this game has tooltips too.
+
I do like that the plot is very brisk and lets you explore quickly without being boggled down with nonsense, even if you didn't skip the lore at the start.
+
Oh, enemies are on the map and have line of sight so you can sneak around them. Though I do feel it's a bit too easy to cheese them.
+
I like the combo move system and that Ennea's MP naturally regenerates, although...
Spoiler:
Observations
=
Oh. Wow. The game has its own installer. A bit much, but alright.
=
I'm seeing quite a few default Moghunter graphics.
=
Ooh. Ow. My computer doesn't like the opening lore cutscene, even with an 8GB upgrade. It stops and starts every so often.
=
Natures from Pokémon are in this? Alright.
=
I am ambivalent towards this voice acting. It's quite wooden but it's not offensive. But it still works better here with the big CG busts than little sprites talking at least.
=
I've gotten like, six potions (not counting the secret one in the chest above Mr. unicorn) before I even go into combat. Quite generous.
=
Aehlevander is the spitting image of
Helios from Sailor Moon
, even down to the fact he's a white-robed man with white hair with a golden crystal in his head that turns into a unicorn.
=
The story is not bad, but it's also not too terribly exciting either. It just feels like generic fantasy fare, especially with all of the "Age of Darkness" talk.
=
We pick up 6 bags of flour for a dude, a task they could have done themselves, and then he gives us his ranch hand to take on an adventure. It feels a bit abrupt, like I didn't get much of a read on this guy's personality.
Spoiler:
Cons
-
(!!)
Oh no... you have all of this custom art yet you stuck to the default RTP sound effects... and default orange bar for HP... and the default font...
-
No keyboard rebinding. A bit more reasonable considering this is MZ, but still.
-
Oh. Uh-oh. I played without skipping the intro story and it seems to have started the actual in-game cutscene, because once the intro ended, it stuck me immediately onto the map with Ennea and her talking unicorn guy without seeing that CG where she's sitting against the water. Oops.
-
(!!!)
The game is VERY resource intensive, as I could barely get 13+ frames even on the map the game starts at. Certain maps drops it down to single digit framerate, which I can only assume is the fault of visual effects + Visustella's obfuscation making the game's job harder than it needs to be.
(In maps without effects and menus, it goes up to 30 frames only, which isn't that much better.)
-
Something I don't like about the compass is that it tells you where treasure chests are, even hidden ones, as well as the fact it doesn't actually highlight exits.
-
Strange how the two arrow buttons on the equipment screen block the text box, but not in Skills.
-
I think it's quite bizarre how you have items on the shelves that can be bought separately from talking to the shopkeeper, but they don't have markers above them to signify to the player that they can even be bought until you rub right up next to them. If
@hiddenone
didn't bring this up, I would never have known.
(Especially since it doesn't seem to be a one-and-done event where you give 100 gold, but another shopkeeper event that ONLY sells the potion while he has potions in his main stock? Very weird, makes me wonder what the point is.)
-
There's a
grass-steppy noise when you run in this specific location
, yet not on the other side.
-
Why does the regular attack of the wolves do 33 damage, but the special charge-up animation Scratch do like, 24? It doesn't make sense to me.
-
Why is the Ground Herb (and other crafting materials) able to be used in combat if it does nothing?
-
(!!)
Not a fan of this combat. I do like the effort put into making it so you can't spam Normal Attack, but the Press Turn Combat system effect where you get an extra turn for nailing enemies with their elemental weakness + stunning them seems quite unbalanced.
Especially since Ennea has regenerating MP so she can keep spamming her moves. I don't have anything against this MP regen effect, but when combined with the Press Turn Combat function, things get pretty mindless.
-
Oh... do the bees have Reflex (aka. auto-dodge physical attacks)? Strange that they don't have a tooltip telling the player about this, especially when you pretty much have to transform to do anything about them as Aehlevander.
-
Auto-battle? Mmmm. I'd rather not have any mechanic that auto-plays the game for me.
-
OH UH. I saw Aehlevander's sprite zip-zoop over the map for a second after killing the forest wolves before his position corrected. Wonder what that's about. (It also happened again when we beat the forest wolves boss.)
It also happened to Ennea's portrait sprite when she talked to Elmir.
-
"It can restore the full HP and MP of whoever drinks its water." sounds pretty strange. I think you should have it say "It can fully restore the HP and MP of whoever drinks from it."
-
The Forest Wolf Boss, as the first boss fight, is quite terrible. It's kind of just mash attack until you beat the boss, since he's a big HP sponge. The minions don't really do anything notable since they get splattered by using Forest Slash (your AOE that stuns them) while the boss wolf himself has so much HP that it makes fighting him a slog.
For reference's sake, it took me 16 turns to kill him. His minions died way before that.
-
THE BOSS HEALS HIMSELF.
NOOOOOOOO
.
He heals for
388(!)
in a fight where you do 70 (unboosted) / 111 (boosted, which is only possible because of the demo-exclusive skill that Aehlevander has). This is a bad decision because bosses that heal themselves are very contentious. If done poorly, it does nothing but extend the boss fight and doesn't really make the fight more interesting.
-
Wouldn't it make sense to just allow the player to enter Master Fennlisher's house if they wanted to? There's not really a point having to talk to the NPCs if you already figured it out / get told where it is explicitly after the first NPC, it just seems like padding.
-
"So many weapons and armor!" feels weird. "So much weaponry and armor" would probably work better.
Spoiler:
Overall Thoughts
Here's the thing. It's a gorgeous game. There's an insane amount of effort on the art side of things.
But there's a lot of little annoying things:
* The continued existence of default RTP sounds and other things like the default font
* The framerate absolutely
SUFFERS
when the game is any map that isn't indoors / in combat. This is likely the fault of the plugins you're using.
* The combat itself being quite easy to break and not all that exciting due to balancing issues. It was pretty dull.
Also, from what I saw of the story, it just seemed like your typical "save the world, young hero" type of fantasy story where you have to fight the dark lord and his underlings. I couldn't get much of a read on the actual personalities of the characters, since they just kind of stayed in their lanes - Aehlevander is the stoic and serious guardian, Ennea is the bold-but-conflicted warrior princess and the farmer guy you got at the end didn't stay long enough to get a read on his personality.
Ennea stood out due to the fact she actually did seem troubled by the state of the world, and her talk with the griffin NPC was somewhat interesting, but it was also quite cryptic. I want to see it actually build into something instead of just being a vague threat.
That said! I am rooting for you to succeed with this, since it's clear you've put in an incredible amount of effort already.

I am ambivalent towards this voice acting. It's quite wooden but it's not offensive. But it still works better here with the big CG busts than little sprites talking at least.
=
I've gotten like, six potions (not counting the secret one in the chest above Mr. unicorn) before I even go into combat. Quite generous.
=
Aehlevander is the spitting image of
Helios from Sailor Moon
, even down to the fact he's a white-robed man with white hair with a golden crystal in his head that turns into a unicorn.
=
The story is not bad, but it's also not too terribly exciting either. It just feels like generic fantasy fare, especially with all of the "Age of Darkness" talk.
=
We pick up 6 bags of flour for a dude, a task they could have done themselves, and then he gives us his ranch hand to take on an adventure. It feels a bit abrupt, like I didn't get much of a read on this guy's personality.
Spoiler:
Cons
-
(!!)
Oh no... you have all of this custom art yet you stuck to the default RTP sound effects... and default orange bar for HP... and the default font...
-
No keyboard rebinding. A bit more reasonable considering this is MZ, but still.
-
Oh. Uh-oh. I played without skipping the intro story and it seems to have started the actual in-game cutscene, because once the intro ended, it stuck me immediately onto the map with Ennea and her talking unicorn guy without seeing that CG where she's sitting against the water. Oops.
-
(!!!)
The game is VERY resource intensive, as I could barely get 13+ frames even on the map the game starts at. Certain maps drops it down to single digit framerate, which I can only assume is the fault of visual effects + Visustella's obfuscation making the game's job harder than it needs to be.
(In maps without effects and menus, it goes up to 30 frames only, which isn't that much better.)
-
Something I don't like about the compass is that it tells you where treasure chests are, even hidden ones, as well as the fact it doesn't actually highlight exits.
-
Strange how the two arrow buttons on the equipment screen block the text box, but not in Skills.
-
I think it's quite bizarre how you have items on the shelves that can be bought separately from talking to the shopkeeper, but they don't have markers above them to signify to the player that they can even be bought until you rub right up next to them. If
@hiddenone
didn't bring this up, I would never have known.
(Especially since it doesn't seem to be a one-and-done event where you give 100 gold, but another shopkeeper event that ONLY sells the potion while he has potions in his main stock? Very weird, makes me wonder what the point is.)
-
There's a
grass-steppy noise when you run in this specific location
, yet not on the other side.
-
Why does the regular attack of the wolves do 33 damage, but the special charge-up animation Scratch do like, 24? It doesn't make sense to me.
-
Why is the Ground Herb (and other crafting materials) able to be used in combat if it does nothing?
-
(!!)
Not a fan of this combat. I do like the effort put into making it so you can't spam Normal Attack, but the Press Turn Combat system effect where you get an extra turn for nailing enemies with their elemental weakness + stunning them seems quite unbalanced.
Especially since Ennea has regenerating MP to just keep using her attacks to keep spamming her moves. I don't have anything against this MP regen effect, but when combined with the Press Turn Combat function, things get pretty mindless.
-
Oh... do the bees have Reflex (aka. auto-dodge physical attacks)? Strange that they don't have a tooltip telling the player about this, especially when you pretty much have to transform to do anything about them as Aehlevander.
-
Auto-battle? Mmmm. I'd rather not have any mechanic that auto-plays the game for me.
-
OH UH. I saw Aehlevander's sprite zip-zoop over the map for a second after killing the forest wolves before his position corrected. Wonder what that's about. (It also happened again when we beat the forest wolves boss.)
It also happened to Ennea's portrait sprite when she talked to Elmir.
-
"It can restore the full HP and MP of whoever drinks its water." sounds pretty strange. I think you should have it say "It can fully restore the HP and MP of whoever drinks from it."
-
The Forest Wolf Boss, as the first boss fight, is quite terrible. It's kind of just mash attack until you beat the boss, since he's a big HP sponge. The minions don't really do anything notable since they get splattered by using Forest Slash (your AOE that stuns them) while the boss wolf himself has so much HP that it makes fighting him a slog.
For reference's sake, it took me 16 turns to kill him. His minions died way before that.
-
THE BOSS HEALS HIMSELF.
NOOOOOOOO
.
He heals for
388(!)
in a fight where you do 70 (unboosted) / 111 (boosted, which is only possible because of the demo-exclusive skill that Aehlevander has). This is a bad decision because bosses that heal themselves are very contentious. If done poorly, it does nothing but extend the boss fight and doesn't really make the fight more interesting.
-
Wouldn't it make sense to just allow the player to enter Master Fennlisher's house if they wanted to? There's not really a point having to talk to the NPCs if you already figured it out / get told where it is explicitly after the first NPC, it just seems like padding.
-
"So many weapons and armor!" feels weird. "So much weaponry and armor" would probably work better.
Spoiler:
Overall Thoughts
Here's the thing. It's a gorgeous game. There's an insane amount of effort on the art side of things.
But there's a lot of little annoying things:
* The continued existence of default RTP sounds and other things like the default font
* The framerate absolutely
SUFFERS
when the game is any map that isn't indoors / in combat. This is likely the fault of the plugins you're using.
* The combat itself being quite easy to break and not all that exciting due to balancing issues. It was pretty dull.
Also, from what I saw of the story, it just seemed like your typical "save the world, young hero" type of fantasy story where you have to fight the dark lord and his underlings. I couldn't get much of a read on the actual personalities of the characters, since they just kind of stayed in their lanes - Aehlevander is the stoic and serious guardian, Ennea is the bold-but-conflicted warrior princess and the farmer guy you got at the end didn't stay long enough to get a read on his personality.
Ennea stood out due to the fact she actually did seem troubled by the state of the world, and her talk with the griffin NPC was somewhat interesting, but it was also quite cryptic. I want to see it actually build into something instead of just being a vague threat.
That said! I am rooting for you to succeed with this, since it's clear you've put in an incredible amount of effort already.
Click to expand...
Thank you so much for the detailed feedback! I appreciate it a lot
I've been thinking about the RTP sound effects for a while. I'm slowly replacing them with custom ones.
I'm also trying my best to find a way to boost the frame rate. The problem is that it works fine on my computer. I have a constant of 50-60 frame rates on most maps, the lowest being 40. I'm still looking into the plugin options to find a better solution, without compensating for the quality of the graphics. Testing everything on my old laptop helps a bit.
Haha, I'm happy you found the resemblance between Aehlevander and Helios. It was intentional. I loved Sailor Moon as a child, especially Helios. So the design of the character is a little tribute. He's going to have a different set of clothes to choose from later in the game.
I'm still working on balancing the battle system and your comments help a lot to get me on the right track! It's probably my main Achilles' heel and I'm still learning from my mistakes.
I hope to adjust the game following your advice and release a bigger demo update sometime in January.
Thank you for playing my game!

posts.author: woootbm
posts.body:
Heya, I played your game briefly and did an impressions video. You can watch it
here
if you are brave! There will be some overlap with some of the points made below, but there's value in hearing reactions to things in real time, too.
Just as a warning, I tend to be one of the harsher critics on here so steel yourself for what's to come.
Some notes up front:
I played the demo on Steam.
I did not encounter any performance issues (although my PC is quite new and has decent hardware like a 4060Ti, IE it is well above standard RM requirements).
Spoiler:
The review
Spoiler:
Positive notes
Character art looks good and is consistent. It also creates a style that makes the elves look like they have a distinct culture.
Mapping is beautiful. My favorite touch are the reflections in the castle and the water.
I just realized this is one of the only RM games that actually understands how rugs work (IE they are not amorphous blobs that take the shape of the room). Thank you!!!
Aehlevander has a hunky, smooth voice.
Combat seems like it could have potential but I didn't get far enough to see.
Dragonbones enemies and custom sprites look great.
Action sequencing looks good and is not over-indulgent.
Overall, the game feels like a professional
(but small indie)
production.
Spoiler:
Neutral/suggestions
I didn't do the side quest to talk to Senersis. I was not given any idea where they are. This does not seem like the type of objective worthy of "you have to figure it out" since our character- presumably- knows this village and where this person lives.
Also there was not any additional tracking for this. If this is an important step, like if it adds a party member or gives important gear, it should have its own quest.
Spoiler:
Negative notes
The lore is beautiful and I appreciate the narrator's efforts to pronounce such complicated names, but there is simply no way I'm retaining this info. This is too much to dump on the player especially since it has so little importance on the immediate story.
Speaking of this narrator, I'm sorry but his mic quality is unacceptable and his read lacks engaging inflection.
The mouth flaps only play briefly and do not follow the length of dialogue.
The chibi sprites are nice but I do not feel they match the rest of the art.
Why does Aehlevander turn into a human? It's cool that he can do that but it seems like most of his combat potential is locked behind turning back into a unicorn, forcing the player to waste a turn at the start of combat.
I appreciate that the player gets to gameplay at a fairly reasonable pace but there is a LOT of it for a first zone.
Ennea's motivation feels vague. It would be a good idea to show what the danger is. An inciting incident that drives her reason to go on this adventure. As it is, it's unclear why she NOW chooses to run off and doesn't create a sense of urgency.
I wanted to mention the encryption method. It only takes me 6 seconds or so to actually get fully into the game, but I saw a comment of it taking someone 5 minutes. Now while I do think that's an outlier, it's worth thinking about the reasons WHY one would do this. I've heard it's to protect plugins from being stolen. But I think this is a very small perspective. This is the same sin as DRM; you are making 99.9% of your players go through hoops just to punish 0.01% of your players. I get that in our small community it seems like a big deal to protect plugin authors but in the WAY LARGER gaming community... no one gives a crap and has no reason to steal them.
